neighbours.label: ' should' addressed to the reader in a role or job description ('As a Business Developer, you should always ...')
fire: As a project manager, you should always keep stakeholders informed about delays.
As a team leader, you should regularly check in with each member of your staff.
As a customer service agent, you should always stay calm with angry callers.
In this role, you should keep in mind that you represent the whole company.
As a junior developer, you should always ask questions when the spec is unclear.
As an account executive, you should build strong relationships with key clients.
In this position you should always follow the safety checklist before each shift.
As a Business Analyst, you should keep in mind the goals of every department.
quiet: As a project manager, I once kept stakeholders waiting for a whole week.
Our team leader regularly checks in with each member of her staff.
The customer service agent stayed calm with the angry caller.
In this role, she represented the whole company at trade fairs.
As a junior developer, he asked many questions about the spec.
The account executive built strong relationships with key clients.
In this position he followed the safety checklist before each shift.
I think we should order pizza tonight instead of cooking.

notes: Probe: 'As a sales manager, you should always' 0.76 was the only strong hit; is needed 0.26, applicants should be able 0.24, work through 0.22, students should have 0.20, casual 'you should try the cake' 0.20 (peak ' try'); 'we should go to the beach' 0.02, 'was able to fix' 0.02, 'must be able to' 0.06. So the test is narrowed to the 'As a <role>, you should' frame.
